notes: Community pack, roadmap Phase 1 candidate. 5 tracks x 10 themes x 5 grade bands = 250 blocks. Expanded by tools/generate_pack.py.

tracks.name: Electricity and the house that carries it

themes.theme: The path from pole to plug
themes.description: Service line, meter, panel, circuit, outlet — the one-way street electricity takes into a home.
themes.transfer_check: Trace and sketch the actual path from your building's meter to one outlet, naming each stage you can safely observe.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where the wire outside connects to your house.
bands.3–5: Trace where power enters your home from outside, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Trace a real power path from pole to a real outlet, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real wiring, the full path from pole to plug.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to trace the real path electricity takes into a home.

themes.theme: The breaker panel is a map
themes.description: What a breaker does, why it trips, and labelling the panel so 3 a.m. problems take one minute.
themes.transfer_check: Test and correctly label every breaker in a real panel, and demonstrate finding the right one for a named outlet.

bands.K–2: Look at the breaker panel with an adult and point at a switch.
bands.3–5: Find one labeled breaker in a real panel, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Read a real breaker panel and identify what each switch controls, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Read and use a real breaker panel confidently, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to read a real breaker panel like a map.

themes.theme: Watts, volts and the kettle that dims the lights
themes.description: Power as a rate, why some appliances are heavy loads, and what an overloaded circuit feels like before it fails.
themes.transfer_check: Rank five real household appliances by wattage from their plates, and identify which two must not share one circuit.

bands.K–2: Notice the lights flicker when a big appliance turns on, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Explain that some appliances use more power than others, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Calculate a real appliance's basic power draw, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real numbers, why a real appliance dims the lights.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real relationship between watts, volts and current.

themes.theme: Cords, plugs and the sockets that scorch
themes.description: Damaged leads, loose sockets, daisy-chained extension strips — the household electrical fires that announce themselves first.
themes.transfer_check: Inspect one real room's cords, plugs and strips against a checklist and remove or report every fault found.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult if a cord looks frayed or damaged.
bands.3–5: Spot a real damaged cord or plug, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real fire hazard from a cord or socket, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Inspect real cords and sockets for hazards on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to spot a real scorched socket or damaged cord.

themes.theme: Water and electricity in the same room
themes.description: Why bathrooms and kitchens have special rules, and what a GFCI/RCD actually detects.
themes.transfer_check: Locate and test every GFCI/RCD protecting wet areas in a real home using its test button, and log the result.

bands.K–2: Never touch a plug with wet hands, with an adult reminding you.
bands.3–5: Explain why water and electricity are dangerous together, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real electrical hazard near water, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Assess a real bathroom or kitchen for electrical-water hazards, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real dangers of water and electricity together.

themes.theme: When the power goes out
themes.description: Reading whether it is your breaker, your building or your street, and the safe order of checks.
themes.transfer_check: Given a staged or real outage, run the diagnostic order — panel, neighbours, provider's outage map — and state the correct next call.

bands.K–2: Stay calm and find an adult when the lights go out.
bands.3–5: Know one safe thing to do during a power outage, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Prepare for a real power outage using a checklist, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Prepare yourself and a household for a real power outage, on your own.
bands.11–12: Lead a real household's power outage preparation and response.

themes.theme: The meter and the bill it writes
themes.description: Reading your own meter, kWh as the unit you are billed in, and matching a month's bill to a month's life.
themes.transfer_check: Read a real meter on two dates, compute the kWh used, and reconcile it against the bill for the same period.

bands.K–2: Look at the numbers on a power meter with an adult.
bands.3–5: Read a simple electricity meter, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Read a real electricity bill and understand its charges, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage a real household's energy costs on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to read and reduce a real energy bill.

themes.theme: Batteries: small, large and dangerous
themes.description: From AA to power bank to e-bike pack — charging habits, swelling cells, and why some batteries must never meet the bin.
themes.transfer_check: Audit the batteries in one household, flag any damaged or swollen cell, and take one to a genuine recycling point.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult before touching any battery you find.
bands.3–5: Learn one safety rule for handling batteries, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real battery hazard and safe handling, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Handle and store real batteries safely on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real hazards and safe handling of different batteries.

themes.theme: Generators, inverters and backup power
themes.description: What can run a fridge overnight, carbon monoxide and the generator that must stay outside, and sizing a backup honestly.
themes.transfer_check: Size a backup source for three named essentials in your home, from their real wattages, and state where it would safely run.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult explain what a generator does.
bands.3–5: Learn what a generator is for, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real safe way to use a generator, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Use a real generator or backup power source safely, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real safety rules for generators and backup power.

themes.theme: Calling the professional
themes.description: The line between owner-safe work and licensed work, and describing an electrical problem so the electrician arrives prepared.
themes.transfer_check: Write the call-out description for one real or staged electrical fault — symptoms, location, panel photo — that a stranger could act on.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who fixes electrical problems.
bands.3–5: Learn when to call an electrician instead of fixing it yourself, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real electrical problem that needs a professional, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Judge, for a real problem, when to call a professional, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real line between DIY and professional electrical work.

tracks.name: Heat, cold and the cost of comfort

themes.theme: Where the heat leaks out
themes.description: Draughts, glazing, loft and wall — the order in which a home loses heat and the cheap fixes that come first.
themes.transfer_check: Survey one real home for heat loss with hands, candle or camera, and rank the three worst leaks with a fix for each.

bands.K–2: Feel for a draft near a window with an adult.
bands.3–5: Find one place where heat escapes a home, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real heat-loss point in a building, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Diagnose and fix a real heat-loss problem in a home, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to find and fix real heat loss in a building.

themes.theme: The heating system you actually have
themes.description: Furnace, boiler, heat pump, resistive — identifying the system, its fuel and its one owner-serviceable part.
themes.transfer_check: Identify a real home's heating type, locate its filter or service point, and perform or schedule the due maintenance.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what makes the house warm in winter.
bands.3–5: Name the type of heating system your home uses, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real heating system's type and how it works, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using a real system, how your home is actually heated.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to identify and understand a real heating system.

themes.theme: Thermostats and the schedule that saves
themes.description: Setbacks, schedules and why heating an empty house is the quietest money leak in the home.
themes.transfer_check: Program a real thermostat with a weekly schedule matched to actual occupancy and estimate the saving from the setback.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult set the thermostat, with their help.
bands.3–5: Read a real thermostat's current setting, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Set a real thermostat schedule that saves energy, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Program a real thermostat schedule that saves real money, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to set a real thermostat schedule for savings.

themes.theme: Hot water: the second-biggest bill
themes.description: Tank versus on-demand, the temperature that scalds versus the temperature that breeds legionella, and the shower's share.
themes.transfer_check: Measure a real tap's hot water temperature, compare it to the safe band, and adjust or report accordingly.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why the shower water gets hot.
bands.3–5: Learn that heating water costs money, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real way to reduce hot water costs, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Reduce your own real household's hot water costs, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why hot water is often the second-biggest energy cost.

themes.theme: Damp, mould and the air a home breathes
themes.description: Condensation versus penetration, extraction fans, and why sealing a home tight without ventilating it grows mould.
themes.transfer_check: Find and diagnose one real damp or condensation site, and apply or specify the ventilation-first remedy.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult if you see a dark spot on a wall.
bands.3–5: Spot a real sign of damp or mould, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real cause of damp or mould in a home, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Diagnose and address real damp or mould in a home, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real causes and fixes for damp and mould.

themes.theme: Keeping cool without drowning the bill
themes.description: Shade, cross-ventilation, fans and when air conditioning earns its cost — heat management as a sequence, not a switch.
themes.transfer_check: Cool one real room through a hot day using a written non-AC sequence first, logging temperatures at each step.

bands.K–2: Use a fan instead of the air conditioner on a mild day, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Name one way to stay cool without high cost, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real affordable cooling strategy, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage real cooling costs in your own household, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on real affordable strategies to stay cool.

themes.theme: The cold snap and the heat wave
themes.description: Frozen pipes, overwhelmed grids and the people most at risk two doors away — extremes as household and neighbourhood events.
themes.transfer_check: Write your household's extreme-temperature plan — pipes, power, and the two neighbours you will check — and rehearse one part.

bands.K–2: Dress warmly or stay in shade when an adult says the weather is extreme.
bands.3–5: Know one safety step for extreme heat or cold, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Prepare for a real extreme weather event using a checklist, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Prepare yourself and a household for a real extreme weather event, on your own.
bands.11–12: Lead a real household's preparation for an extreme heat or cold event.

themes.theme: Fuel poverty and the help that exists
themes.description: When heat competes with food: tariffs, grants, insulation schemes and the entitlements that go unclaimed.
themes.transfer_check: Map the energy-cost support available at your own address — programs, eligibility, application route — into a half-page guide.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens if a family can't pay to keep warm.
bands.3–5: Learn that some families struggle to pay for heat, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real assistance program for energy costs, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Find and apply for real energy assistance for a household in need, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else to real assistance programs for fuel poverty.

themes.theme: Reading an efficiency label
themes.description: Energy ratings on appliances and homes: what the letters measure, and lifetime cost versus sticker price.
themes.transfer_check: Compare two real appliances by projected lifetime energy cost and defend a purchase choice with the arithmetic shown.

bands.K–2: Look at a sticker on a new appliance with an adult.
bands.3–5: Find the efficiency rating on a real appliance, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Read a real efficiency label and what it means for cost, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Use real efficiency labels to make a real purchasing decision, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to read a real efficiency label correctly.

themes.theme: The retrofit, in the right order
themes.description: Insulate, seal, ventilate, then upgrade the heat source — why the order matters and what each step costs and saves.
themes.transfer_check: Draft a sequenced retrofit plan for a real dwelling with rough costs, and justify why your step one comes first.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what order to fix things in an old house.
bands.3–5: Name one home improvement that saves energy, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify the real correct order of energy retrofit steps, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan a real energy retrofit in the correct order, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on the real correct order for an energy retrofit.

tracks.name: The grid: where power comes from

themes.theme: The machine the size of a country
themes.description: Generation, transmission, distribution — the grid as one synchronised machine that must balance every second.
themes.transfer_check: Explain to someone else, with a drawing, why the grid must match supply to demand instantly and what happens when it cannot.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how electricity gets to every house.
bands.3–5: Learn that power plants connect to every home, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain how a real regional grid connects power plants to homes, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real infrastructure, how the grid works as one machine.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how the real grid functions as a country-sized machine.

themes.theme: The sources and their trade-offs
themes.description: Coal, gas, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar — what each costs, emits, and does when the wind drops or the river runs low.
themes.transfer_check: Build an honest one-page comparison of three generation sources using published capacity and emissions data.

bands.K–2: Name one way electricity is made, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Name two ways electricity can be made, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Compare two real energy sources and their trade-offs, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Compare real energy sources' trade-offs using real evidence, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real trade-offs across major energy sources.

themes.theme: Your region's actual mix
themes.description: Finding the real-time generation mix where you live, and how it shifts by hour and season.
themes.transfer_check: Pull your region's live or published generation mix on two different days and explain one difference between them.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what kind of power plant is near your home.
bands.3–5: Learn what real sources power your area, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify your real region's actual energy mix, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research and explain your real region's actual energy mix, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real evidence behind your region's energy mix.

themes.theme: Peak hours and the duck curve
themes.description: Why evening demand is expensive, what solar does to the daytime curve, and when a kWh is cheapest to use.
themes.transfer_check: Shift two real household loads off peak hours for a week and show the timing change (and saving, where tariffs allow).

bands.K–2: Notice when your family uses the most electricity, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn that power use changes throughout the day, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real peak usage period and why it matters, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real data, what the duck curve shows about grid demand.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real challenge the duck curve poses for grids.

themes.theme: Storage: the missing piece
themes.description: Batteries, pumped hydro and why storing electricity at scale is the grid's hardest problem.
themes.transfer_check: Calculate how long a named home battery could run your fridge and lights from their real wattages, and compare to a real outage duration.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why a flashlight needs batteries stored up.
bands.3–5: Explain what energy storage is for, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real grid-scale storage technology and its role, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real examples, why storage is the grid's missing piece.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real state of grid-scale energy storage.

themes.theme: Blackouts, brownouts and how grids fail
themes.description: Cascading failure, load shedding and the famous outages — what actually went wrong and what changed after.
themes.transfer_check: Take one documented major blackout, map its failure chain, and identify the step where intervention could have stopped it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens when too many things use power at once.
bands.3–5: Learn the difference between a blackout and a brownout, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real cause of a grid failure, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using a real event, how and why a grid actually failed.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real mechanisms behind grid failures.

themes.theme: Rooftops that generate
themes.description: Home solar honestly: orientation, payback, export tariffs and the sales pitches that skip the denominator.
themes.transfer_check: Assess a real roof for solar — orientation, shading, rough yield — and produce a payback estimate you can defend.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what solar panels on a roof do.
bands.3–5: Learn that some roofs make their own power, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain how a real rooftop solar system works, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real rooftop solar option for a home, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on real rooftop generation options and their trade-offs.

themes.theme: The electric vehicle and the house
themes.description: Charging levels, what an EV does to a home's load, and the car battery as future grid storage.
themes.transfer_check: Plan home charging for a named EV on a real electrical service — charger level, circuit, schedule — within the panel's capacity.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if a car can plug into the wall like a phone.
bands.3–5: Learn that electric cars charge at home, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real requirement for home electric vehicle charging, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real home's readiness for electric vehicle charging, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on real home charging setup for an electric vehicle.

themes.theme: Who pays for the wires
themes.description: Standing charges, network costs and why your bill has lines that are not energy — the grid as shared infrastructure.
themes.transfer_check: Decompose one real energy bill line by line and explain, in plain words, what each charge pays for.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who pays to build the power lines.
bands.3–5: Learn that the wires cost money to build and maintain, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify who real grid infrastructure costs fall on, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real billing, how grid infrastructure costs are recovered.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real economics of who pays for the grid.

themes.theme: The transition, without the slogans
themes.description: Decarbonising a grid: what is genuinely hard, what is already solved, and how to read claims from every side.
themes.transfer_check: Take one energy-transition claim from current media, check it against grid data, and deliver a verdict with sources.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if the way we make electricity is changing.
bands.3–5: Learn that energy sources are changing over time, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real fact about the energy transition, without slogans, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain the real energy transition honestly, weighing real trade-offs.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real energy transition, evidence over slogans.

tracks.name: Water, gas and the other pipes

themes.theme: The stopcock and the sixty seconds that matter
themes.description: Where water enters, how to shut it off, and why every household member should be able to do it in the dark.
themes.transfer_check: Locate and operate the main water shutoff in a real dwelling, then time a second household member doing it cold.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where the water shut-off is at home.
bands.3–5: Find the real water shut-off valve, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Locate and operate a real stopcock quickly, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Shut off real water quickly in an emergency, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else why finding the stopcock in advance actually matters.

themes.theme: The drip that becomes a flood
themes.description: Reading early leak signs — stains, warping, the spinning meter with everything off — and the escalation each deserves.
themes.transfer_check: Run a whole-home leak check including the meter-still test, and document findings with photos.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult if you see a dripping pipe.
bands.3–5: Notice a real small leak before it gets worse, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real leak's severity and urgency, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Diagnose and respond to a real leak before it floods, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why a real small drip can become a real flood.

themes.theme: Drains: what goes down and what must not
themes.description: Fats, wipes and the fatberg economy; the trap under every sink and the smell that means it has failed.
themes.transfer_check: Clear or demonstrate clearing a real trap safely, and write the household's what-not-to-flush rules on one card.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what should never go down the drain.
bands.3–5: Name one thing that shouldn't go down a drain, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real substance that damages real drains, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage real household drain use responsibly, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else what real substances never belong in a drain.

themes.theme: Gas: the smell that is a command
themes.description: What natural gas smells like and why, the do-nots (switches, flames, phones indoors), and the evacuation-then-call order.
themes.transfer_check: Recite and walk the gas-leak response for your own home, including where the gas shutoff is and the number called from outside.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult right away if you smell something like rotten eggs.
bands.3–5: Know that a gas smell means leave immediately, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Respond correctly to a real gas smell, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Respond correctly and quickly to a real gas leak smell, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else why a real gas smell is a command, not a suggestion.

themes.theme: Carbon monoxide: the one with no smell
themes.description: Where CO comes from, the symptoms mistaken for flu, and the alarm that is not optional.
themes.transfer_check: Verify working CO alarms in the right locations of a real home, test them, and fix or escalate any gap.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why a house needs a special alarm besides a smoke alarm.
bands.3–5: Learn that carbon monoxide has no smell, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real carbon monoxide risk and detector need, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Ensure a real home has working carbon monoxide protection, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real danger of an odourless gas like carbon monoxide.

themes.theme: Water heaters, boilers and the annual visit
themes.description: The service schedule that keeps combustion appliances safe, and the signs (soot, yellow flame, pilot outages) that cannot wait.
themes.transfer_check: Check a real combustion appliance for the visible warning signs and confirm or book its service record.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why the water heater needs to be checked sometimes.
bands.3–5: Learn that heaters need regular checks, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify what a real annual boiler or heater check involves, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Schedule and understand a real annual maintenance visit, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why a real annual check on a heater matters.

themes.theme: Hard water, soft water and what scale does
themes.description: Mineral content, kettle fur, dying heating elements — and whether treatment is worth it where you live.
themes.transfer_check: Test or look up your local water hardness and inspect one real appliance for scale, recommending treat or tolerate with reasons.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why a kettle sometimes has white bits inside.
bands.3–5: Learn what hard water leaves behind, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify real scale buildup and its cause, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage real hard water effects in a home, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else what real hard water does to pipes and appliances.

themes.theme: Sewage, septic and where it all goes
themes.description: Mains drainage versus septic, what a treatment plant does, and the household's end of the bargain.
themes.transfer_check: Trace where your own wastewater actually goes — to which works or tank — and list the two household behaviours that most protect it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where the toilet water goes.
bands.3–5: Learn where wastewater goes after flushing, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Trace a real sewage or septic system's path, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real infrastructure, how a real septic or sewage system works.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real difference between sewage and septic systems.

themes.theme: The utility bill quartet
themes.description: Water, gas, electric, connectivity: metering, estimated bills, and catching the error that repeats every month.
themes.transfer_check: Audit a household's four utility bills for one quarter, verify each against meters or usage, and dispute or explain any anomaly.

bands.K–2: Look at a stack of bills with an adult and count them.
bands.3–5: Name the different utility bills a home might get, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Read a real set of utility bills and their charges, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage a real household's full set of utility bills, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on managing a real quartet of utility bills.

themes.theme: Turning a home off and on again
themes.description: The vacancy checklist: what gets shut, drained and unplugged before an absence, and the restart order that avoids surprises.
themes.transfer_check: Write and execute (or fully rehearse) the shutdown and restart checklist for a real dwelling before and after an absence.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens when a family moves into a new home.
bands.3–5: Learn that utilities need to be turned on when moving in, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify the real steps to activate utilities in a new home, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Set up real utilities for a new home on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through real utility setup and shutdown for a move.

themes.theme: Finding the hogs
themes.description: Measuring what each appliance really draws — the heaters, dryers and always-on boxes that dominate a bill.
themes.transfer_check: Meter or plate-audit ten real appliances, rank them by monthly cost, and name the top three with figures.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult which appliance uses the most electricity.
bands.3–5: Guess which real appliance uses the most power, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real energy-hungry appliance in a home, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Find and address a real high-energy appliance's usage, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to find the real biggest energy users in a home.

themes.theme: Standby: the load that never sleeps
themes.description: Phantom draw across a modern home — what it sums to over a year and which devices deserve a true off.
themes.transfer_check: Measure or estimate your home's total standby load, then eliminate part of it and show the before-and-after.

bands.K–2: Turn off a device instead of leaving it plugged in, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn that plugged-in devices use power even when off, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real standby power drain and reduce it, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Reduce real standby power use across a household, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how real standby power adds up over time.

themes.theme: Light: the solved problem
themes.description: LED economics, lumens versus watts, and the fixtures still burning money in most buildings.
themes.transfer_check: Survey one building's lighting, compute the payback of converting what remains, and convert at least one fixture.

bands.K–2: Turn off a light when leaving a room, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Compare a real old bulb to a real efficient one, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real efficient lighting choice and its savings, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Convert a real home's lighting to efficient options, on your own.

themes.theme: The laundry equation
themes.description: Temperature, load size and the dryer's outsized cost — the washing habits that halve the energy per clean shirt.
themes.transfer_check: Run one week's laundry under changed rules (full loads, lower temp, line-dry where possible) and quantify the difference.

bands.K–2: Help sort laundry by color with an adult.
bands.3–5: Help choose a real efficient laundry setting, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Choose real efficient laundry settings and timing, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Run real household laundry efficiently, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real cost trade-offs in laundry choices.

themes.theme: The kitchen's energy order
themes.description: Kettle, microwave, hob, oven — matching the tool to the job, and the lids, batch bakes and fridge habits that add up.
themes.transfer_check: Cook one meal twice — habitual versus energy-ordered — and compare the measured or estimated energy of each.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult which is faster, a microwave or an oven.

bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real energy order of common cooking methods.

themes.theme: One degree and one hour
themes.description: What a single thermostat degree and a single heating hour actually cost across a season — small levers, honestly sized.

bands.K–2: Notice that a warmer or cooler setting changes comfort, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn that a small thermostat change saves energy, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Calculate a real saving from one degree or one hour of setback, with a checker.

bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real math behind small thermostat changes.

themes.theme: Reading your own usage curve
themes.description: Smart meter data and bill histories as a diary of the household — spotting the anomaly, the season and the habit in the graph.

bands.K–2: Look at a chart of energy use with an adult.

bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to read and act on a real usage curve.

themes.theme: The tariff you are actually on
themes.description: Flat, time-of-use, prepay — what you are on, what you should be on, and switching without being switched.

bands.11–12: Advise someone else on choosing a real tariff suited to their usage.
